blocks.text: Lots and land in Central Abbotsford
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple infill parcels are the default land form: The central area mixes older single detached streets (RS3, RS5 and infill RS3-i / RS7 zones) with the city's deepest strata stock. A vacant or teardown parcel on those streets is a fee-simple lot: the buyer's own title, no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fee — zoning, the two neighbourhood plans and any registered covenants govern what can replace the existing house.

Lot character: RS3 minimum interior lot 540 m²; RS5 minimum interior lot 420 m²; and RS7 (Infill Residential Zone) minimum lot size 300 m² for new interior lots, with minimum lot width 10.0 m and depth 22.5 m — among the smallest detached lot minimums in the city. RS3-i (Urban Residential Zone, Infill) is named in City council material for Maple Street in the Historic Downtown plan area.

A September 16, 2025 City council report (PDS 172-2025) processes a rezoning of 2330 Fir Street (Lots 30 and 31) from RS3-i to RS7 to facilitate a three-lot subdivision, consistent with the Urban 3 – Infill designation — with the standard conditions in that report being a development agreement / cash-in-lieu for road and utility upgrades under the Development Bylaw, a Community Amenity Contribution, a s.219 covenant limiting density on the new lots, and resolution of unbudgeted funding items.
Do not present Rail District ground as buyable lots.
Built-form developments — not land: They confirm the core builds UP on its land; none sells lots.
The core's presales (Rail District phases, Mahogany) sell homes.

blocks.text: Where lots come up and what to know

items.t: The City's own commercial study describes the City Centre as a roughly rectangular area bordered approximately by Peardonville Road and Mill Lake to the south; Ware Street, Mill Lake Road and Horn Street to the east; Parkview Street and Tims Street to the west; and to the north by a line roughly parallel to George Ferguson Way and Maclure Road, centred on South Fraser Way. The Historic Downtown plan's focused redevelopment area is bounded in plan material by Pine Street, Cyril Street, McDougall Avenue and McCallum Road.

Where land actually trades: there is no greenfield ground in the core. Land changes hands as (1) individual infill / teardown parcels on the older detached streets, (2) small subdivisions carved out of those streets through rezoning, and (3) development sites assembled for the plan-designated multi-family forms — the Rail District being the named example.

Schools physically in the central area (SD34 sites): Godson Elementary (33130 Bevan Ave), Dormick Park Elementary (32161 Dormick Avenue), Abbotsford Middle and Abbotsford Senior Secondary. Two settled locator chains are carried in.

Zoning: Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 governs. The land-relevant central zones are RS3 (minimum interior lot 540 m²), RS5 (420 m²), RS7 Infill (300 m² minimum, 10.0 m width, 22.5 m depth) and RS3-i infill. In the core, the zone plus the neighbourhood-plan designation — not the street's current houses — decides a parcel's real value.

Plans: two neighbourhood plans inside Abbotsforward 2050: The City Centre Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2913-2019) and the Historic Downtown Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2920-2019) are the adopted plans for the core, under Abbotsforward 2050 — Abbotsford's CURRENT Official Community Plan, adopted December 2025. Historic Downtown designations that price land: Urban 1 – Midrise (up to 6 storeys), Urban Centre – Mixed Use, Urban 2 – Ground Oriented (rowhouses, townhouse, multiplex or duplex housing) and Urban 3 – Infill (single detached with some ground-oriented duplexes). Abbotsforward 2050 also states a new mixed-use centre between the hospital and Mill Lake Park and a Primary Transit Corridor along South Fraser Way between Clearbrook and McCallum Road.

SSMUH / added units on a lot: the bylaw's s.140 small-scale multi-unit provision allows 3 units on lots 280 m² or less and 4 units on lots greater than 280 m² under its stated conditions, and s.140.3.8 permits one secondary suite in all single detached dwellings. Abbotsford's suite cap is under 50% of the principal dwelling, and a coach/garden suite is capped at 15% of lot area to a maximum of 100 m². This 3–4-unit provision is the core's main lot-value lever: a teardown parcel's price is routinely its unit count, so the s.140 conditions must be read for the specific lot before paying for potential.
Heritage diligence: the Gur Sikh Temple (Abbotsford Sikh Temple) at 33089 South Fraser Way is a designated National Historic Site in the core.

If a lot were bare-land strata (no known case in the core): the BC strata block would apply to the LOT — Form B diligence (fee, approved levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 plus up to 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions).
The core's smallest-lot zone is also its rezoning story. Small-lot does not automatically mean maximum-density: read the covenants registered on the new titles.

The Rail District's 19 acres are the exception that proves the core's rule. One developer assembling 19 acres in Historic Downtown is newsworthy precisely because central land otherwise trades parcel by parcel. The assembly sells townhomes and apartments (The Abby Townhome Series, The Mason) — a land buyer cannot buy into it lot by lot.
The growth arrow in the current plan points at a gap, not a field. Parcels on that seam carry plan value that their current houses do not show.

A "Central Abbotsford" land label in a feed may not be central at all. The King Road cluster (34248 King Road) is filed under Central Abbotsford, Poplar and Abbotsford East by different feeds for the same address. For land diligence the PID, the zone and the plan designation are the stable identifiers.

items.t: Nearby areas: Abbotsford West to the west, Abbotsford East to the east, Poplar to the northwest.

Main roads named in City plan material: South Fraser Way (the commercial backbone), George Ferguson Way, McCallum Road, Clearbrook Road, Ware Street and Old Yale Road, with Highway 1 interchanges at McCallum Road and Clearbrook Road serving the central area.

Where the mobile-home stock in this sub-area sits: the one park, Georgian Park, is on Horn Street at the east edge of the City Centre frame above — Horn Street is named in that frame as an east-edge street.

Transit: Bourquin Exchange is in the central area; BC Transit Central Fraser Valley routes named in service material include 1 (Highstreet/UFV), 2 (Highstreet/McMillan), 4 (Saddle/Montrose), 5 (Clearbrook/Bourquin via Hospital), 12 (UFV/Bourquin), 17 (Industrial/Bourquin), 21 (Aldergrove/Abbotsford) and 31 (Abbotsford/Mission).

Schools physically in the central area, on SD34 school sites: Godson Elementary (33130 Bevan Ave), Dormick Park Elementary (32161 Dormick Avenue), Abbotsford Middle (33231 Bevan Avenue) and Abbotsford Senior Secondary (33355 Bevan Ave).

blocks.text: Central Abbotsford: streets and boundaries

items.t: Central Abbotsford is the city core centred on South Fraser Way, not a single official City neighbourhood.
The Historic Downtown focused redevelopment area is bounded by Pine Street, Cyril Street, McDougall Avenue and McCallum Road.
Abbotsford West lies to the west, Abbotsford East to the east, and Poplar to the northwest.

blocks.text: Central Abbotsford: the housing stock

items.t: The core mixes older detached streets with the city's deepest strata stock around South Fraser Way.
Mahogany at Mill Lake, 2180 Gladwin Road, is a 27-storey concrete tower of 152 suites by Quantum Properties beside Mill Lake.
Detached minimums here include RS7 infill lots down to 300 m², with 10.0 m width and 22.5 m depth.

blocks.text: Central Abbotsford: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The small-scale multi-unit housing amendment is Bylaw No. 3560-2024, adopted June 25, 2024.
Historic Downtown designations include Urban 1 – Midrise up to 6 storeys and Urban 2 – Ground Oriented for rowhouses, townhouses, multiplexes or duplexes.

blocks.text: Central Abbotsford: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Four public schools share the Bevan Avenue corridor in the core. Godson Elementary is at 33130 Bevan Avenue, Dormick Park Elementary at 32161 Dormick Avenue, Abbotsford Middle at 33231 Bevan Avenue and Abbotsford Senior Secondary at 33355 Bevan Avenue.
Mill Lake Park is accessed from Bevan Avenue and Emerson Street, and Centennial Outdoor Pool is at 2310 Emerson Street.
Clearbrook Library is at 32320 George Ferguson Way, and the Abbotsford library branch shares 33355 Bevan Avenue with Abbotsford Senior Secondary.
The Gur Sikh Temple at 33089 South Fraser Way is designated a National Historic Site and is described by Parks Canada as the oldest surviving Gurdwara.

blocks.text: Central Abbotsford: costs and taxes

items.t: Abbotsford's 2026 residential tax rate is set by Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3727-2026, expressed per $1,000 of taxable value.
For Class 1 residential, the bylaw's Table 1 components are 1.08284, 1.78296, 0.08582, 0.11583 and 0.08836 per $1,000.
Water and sewer customers are billed bi-monthly, except Clearbrook Waterworks District customers, who are billed quarterly for sewer.
Starting January 2027, solid waste fees move onto the utility bill alongside water and sewer and no longer appear on the annual Property Tax Notice.
The City of Abbotsford is listed by the Province as a designated taxable area for the Speculation and Vacancy Tax, so owners must complete the annual declaration.

blocks.text: Central Abbotsford: getting around

items.t: Bourquin Exchange is the central transit exchange. BC Transit Central Fraser Valley routes named for the core include 1 (Highstreet/University of the Fraser Valley), 2, 4, 5 (Clearbrook/Bourquin via Hospital), 12, 17 and 21 (Aldergrove/Abbotsford).
Highway 11 north from the core leads to Mission.

blocks.text: Central Abbotsford: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check floodplain status lot by lot in the City WebMap, even in the upland core. Willband Creek runs through the Historic Downtown and central area, and the City flood page separates this area from Sumas Prairie without clearing any single parcel.
Check the plan designation before a rebuild in Historic Downtown, because Urban 1, Urban 2 and Urban 3 designations set different expected forms.
Confirm Agricultural Land Reserve status in the Official Community Plan maps and WebMap for any edge lot; no central parcel was confirmed as ALR-free here.

faq.a: Not from a subdivision or a lot release — none exists in the core. What you can buy is an individual infill or teardown parcel on the older detached streets (fee-simple), priced on its RS3/RS5/RS7 zoning and its plan designation, or — as a developer — assembled ground like the Rail District site, which is a master-plan land play, not lot inventory.
faq.q: Can I buy a bare lot in Central Abbotsford?

faq.a: RS7 (Infill Residential Zone) allows new interior lots down to 300 m², with minimum width 10.0 m and depth 22.5 m; RS3 minimum interior lot is 540 m² and RS5 is 420 m². But reaching RS7 usually takes a rezoning — the documented Fir Street route rezoned RS3-i to RS7 for a three-lot subdivision, with servicing, amenity and covenant conditions attached.
faq.q: How small can a new central lot be?

faq.a: Usually its unit potential: s.140 allows 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less and 4 units on lots over 280 m² in the stated conditions, one secondary suite is permitted in all single detached dwellings (s.140.3.8), and the plan designations (Urban 2 – Ground Oriented; Urban 1 – Midrise to 6 storeys) set the larger forms. Confirm the zone section and designation for the parcel before paying for any of it.
faq.q: What is an older central house actually worth as land?

faq.a: It turns on the seller and the parcel's history, per CRA GI-003: an individual's sale of personal-use land is generally exempt, but a sale in the course of a business or of a parcel created by subdividing into more than two parts can be taxable. A developer-sold newly created lot is the taxable pattern; a long-held family lot usually is not. Have the contract allocate the GST expressly.
faq.q: Do I pay GST on a teardown or a subdivided lot?

faq.a: A park's age rule lives in its park rules and tenancy documents, not in a strata bylaw, so the written park rules are the deciding document; the Province's general park rule is that in a designated 55-plus park at least one tenant on the site must be 55 or older. Get the park's current rule in writing.
What is known is the form class — individual duplexes on single lots, with the Historic Downtown plan's Urban 2 and Urban 3 designations expressly enabling duplex housing on qualifying lots.
faq.q: Is there a duplex development in Central Abbotsford I can buy into?

faq.a: Neither — it is a pad-rental manufactured home park at its guide mobile home: You would own the home as a chattel and rent the pad; you would not own land, and the mhpta — not the Strata Property Act — governs.
faq.q: Is Georgian Park a strata or bare-land purchase?

faq.a: Match the lot to the zone first: RS3 needs 540 m², RS5 needs 420 m², and RS7 infill lots go down to 300 m² (10.0 m width, 22.5 m depth) — among the smallest detached lot minimums in the city — but zone and stated conditions decide, so confirm the zone section before paying for potential.
faq.q: What lot size do I need to subdivide or infill?

faq.a: Two adopted neighbourhood plans govern the core. The City Centre Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2913-2019) and the Historic Downtown Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2920-2019) sit under Abbotsforward 2050, and a buyer should check which plan area the lot falls in before assuming height or form.

Yes, one secondary suite is permitted in all single detached dwellings. Zoning Bylaw s.140.3.8 states the permission, subject to bylaw conditions including size limits, so a buyer should confirm the suite meets the current section before counting rental use.
faq.q: Can a detached home here have a suite?

faq.a: Enter the primary home address in the School District 34 (SD34) School Locator.
faq.q: How is the school catchment checked?

faq.a: Both test addresses return the same chain. 33130 Bevan Avenue returns Godson Elementary, Abbotsford Middle and Abbotsford Senior Secondary, and 32161 Dormick Avenue returns Dormick Park Elementary with the same middle and secondary schools.
faq.q: What did the locator return for central test addresses?

faq.a: The City flood page describes Sumas Prairie as low-lying agricultural land in East Abbotsford, a separate area from the central upland; parcel-level floodplain status for a central address requires a City floodplain map check.
faq.q: Is Central Abbotsford in the Sumas Prairie floodplain?
